identity.title: Chebyshev Policies and the Mountain Car Problem: Reinforcement Learning for Low-Dimensional Control Tasks

problem.claim: Analytically solve the Mountain Car reinforcement-learning benchmark and derive its optimal control solution.

gap.claim: The authors report that an optimal analytical solution had remained unavailable for 36 years.

contributions.claim: An analytical optimal-control solution for Mountain Car.
Chebyshev policies, introduced from first principles as a universal dense class of RL policies.
Evaluation of Chebyshev policies across additional RL tasks, including a real-world nonlinear motion-control testbed.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Chebyshev policies as a first-principles universal dense policy class motivated by the derived optimal control.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the optimal control is simple while modern RL agents remain substantially suboptimal.
As drop-in replacements for neural networks, Chebyshev policies are reported to reduce regret by a factor of 4.18 while using 277 times fewer parameters.
Across further tasks, the authors report consistent performance improvements over neural networks with PPO, ARS, and REINFORCE.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper analytically solves Mountain Car and derives an optimal control solution.
The authors use the solution to highlight the simplicity of optimal control and the large gap of modern RL agents from optimality.
They introduce Chebyshev policies as a universal dense policy class motivated by the analysis.
The policies are tested as neural-network replacements on additional RL tasks and a real-world nonlinear motion-control testbed.
The authors report consistent improvements over neural networks paired with PPO, ARS, and REINFORCE.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links an analytically derived simple optimum to both a diagnosis of agent suboptimality and the design of a lightweight policy class.

lessons.interpretation: A tractable benchmark solution can serve as a design guide, not only as an evaluation target.
lessons.application: For a low-dimensional control paper, derive or characterize the target optimum first, then use its structure to motivate the policy parameterization.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the optimum is analytically inaccessible or its structure does not transfer beyond the benchmark.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the Mountain Car assumptions, derivation details, or meaning and measurement conditions of the reported regret factor.
It does not provide task-level scores, statistical variation, training budgets, or details of the real-world testbed.
The basis, implementation, and scope of the claimed universal density are not detailed in the abstract.
